labels.quote: The aesthetic choices, from the set design to the visual effects, fail to create a compelling or immersive world.
I think there's too many characters and not enough time to explore each character.
The lack of a coherent plot makes it difficult to stay invested, and the film quickly becomes tedious.
I loved the direction he took.
It lacks an action part where the Joker and Harley Quinn drown the city in chaos.
The result is a convoluted, overlong, often-uninteresting offering that’s heavy on style but weak on substance and not especially interesting.
I thought the story was good, the acting was fine and the special effects were done well and more grounded and gritty than your normal super hero movies.

'Red One' is perhaps slightly overlong and I didn't sense much chemistry between the cast, though those onscreen still give enjoyable performances and the plot is suitably entertaining whilst giving the necessary Xmas vibes.
While the actors clearly enjoy playing off each other, the story itself is expectedly generic, relying heavily on predictable holiday tropes.
Dialogue lacks wit or charm, with most performances coming across as forced, almost like actors reciting homework.
The cinematography, sadly, doesn't help either, with over-reliance on weak CGI and clumsy action sequences that fail to impress.
There are still some jokes aimed at the cold-hearted adult who will inevitably be dragged along on the family cinema outing.
Some scenes dragged on while others were cut far shorter.
Needlessly long, boring and utterly useless Oscar bait.
